newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent ends weaker but well supported.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent ends weaker but well supported.

text.p: IPE Brent futures ended weaker depressed by weaker NYMEX products and pre-weekend profit taking, but found support at the lower levels, traders said.
"People were reluctant to sell the market too low," one trader said "Heat still looks like it's go plenty of room to rise despite today's poor performance".
The January Brent contract last traded 28 cents lower at $23.32 a barrel. December WTI ended 26 cents off at $24.24, while January was off 25 cents at $24.10.
Traders said Brent had just bounced sideways looking for fresh direction, finding support at $23.30 and $23.35 a barrel.
December gas oil settled $1.50 up at $220.75 a tonne, off earlier highs of $221.50 with NYMEX December heating oil trading around around one cent a gallon lower at the London close.
Bullish sentiment in Europe for gas oil was reinforced by talk that the trading house with the bulk of the record 865,100 tonne delivery already had homes for the material, most of it outside Europe.
However, physical traders were sceptical. "It all depends on the long, if 200,000-300,000 tonnes comes onto the market premiums, (to the IPE) will collapse," one said
